title: Fill the empty boxes
intro: `new` builds the boxes, and Java never leaves one empty: every box starts at its type's default value. Pick the value each new array starts with.

rounds.right: Numbers start at zero: every box of a new `int[]` holds `0`.

why.0.0: `0.0` is a `double`. An `int` box holds whole numbers, so its zero is plain `0`.
why.null: `null` means "no object", and only a reference can hold it. `int` is a primitive type: its boxes hold numbers, and a number starts at zero.
why.*: Only the primitive types get a zero-like default, and `int` is one of them: its boxes start at zero.

rounds.right: A new `boolean[]` is all `false`: nothing has been switched on yet.

why.0: Java's booleans are not numbers, so a `boolean` box can't hold `0`. Its zero-like default is one of the two values a boolean can hold.
why.null: `null` is only for references, and `boolean` is a primitive type: its boxes hold `true` or `false`, and a new one starts as the one that means "not yet".
why.*: A `boolean` box can only hold `true` or `false`, and a new one starts as `false`.

rounds.right: `String` is an object type, so each box holds a reference, and a reference to nothing is `null`.

why.\"\": An empty String is still an object, and `new String[{size}]` makes no objects at all: just {size} boxes for references. A reference to nothing is `null`.
why.*: Only the primitive types get a zero-like default. `String` is an object type, so its boxes hold references (arrows), and every reference starts as `null`.

rounds.right: A `double` starts at zero too, written `0.0`: that's how Java prints a double's zero.

why.0: Nearly: it is zero, but the box holds a `double`, and Java writes a double's zero with a decimal point.
why.null: `null` is only for references, and `double` is a primitive type: its boxes hold numbers, and they start at zero.
why.*: `double` is a primitive number type, so its boxes start at zero, written as a double.

rounds.right: A new `char` box holds `'\u0000'`, the invisible NUL character. Print it and you see nothing at all; its number is 0.

why.' ': A space is a real character you can type (its number is 32). A new `char` box holds something less: the invisible character whose number is 0.
why.0: Close: its number is 0, but the box holds a `char`, so its value is written as a character literal in single quotes.
why.\"\": `""` is an empty String, an object. A `char` box holds one primitive character, and a new one holds the character whose number is 0.
why.null: `null` is only for references, and `char` is a primitive type. Its default is a character: the one whose number is 0.
why.*: A `char` box holds one character, and a new one starts as the invisible NUL character, `'\u0000'`.
